title: SELLAS jumped 156% yesterday on Phase 3 data — then filed a $150million offering. Victory lap, or a dilution trap?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
\[SLS\]([https://tickeron.com/ticker/SLS/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/SLS/)) went from Monday's close of  
$7.47 to $19.09 in Tuesday's regular session, about +156%, after  
opening as high as $24.11. The catalyst was topline Phase 3 REGAL  
data: cancer vaccine galinpepimut-S cut the risk of death by 41% in  
second-remission AML, with median overall survival of 24.0 months  
versus 14.7 months (HR 0.59, p=0.035).  
  
That print was Nov 17, not today. After the close, SELLAS launched a  
$150 million stock offering, and the shares were knocked around in  
after-hours and into today. Treat the $19.09 figure as yesterday's  
close, not a live quote.  
  
The Phase 3 write-up, with the survival numbers:  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-sellas-life-sciences-group-sls-stock-up-157-03-today-39901/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-sellas-life-sciences-group-sls-stock-up-157-03-today-39901/)  
  
Is the offering just funding a real breakthrough, or does the dilution  
cap what that data is worth from here?  
  
Not financial advice. Figures are from Tuesday's write-up, not live quotes.
